newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Dec 20.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

Comment -- Trading warmed up Wednesday after a slow start on Monday and Tuesday, stabilizing some prices and bringing others back at least part of the way from early-week lows, Random Lengths said in its weekly review. The pickup in activity started with wholesalers covering short positions, it said.

Wholesalers were then joined on Thursday by distributors, dealers and treaters filling orders they needed to place prior to the holidays. To get the ball rolling, mills often had to discount floor stock substantially, the reporting agency said.
But producers were quick to raise prices on items where they accumulated enough orders to take them into holiday shutdowns.
Some buyers shopped blocks for post-holiday delivery but mills usually turned down the steep counters attached, it said.
A cold front across the upper Midwest and into the South slowed shipments and restrained buying enthusiasm. Some saw Tuesday's strong Nov housing starts as proof of new year demand.
But other dealers concluded the Nov starts were inflated by seasonal factors and declined to react to the news, it said.

With the amount of Canadian lumber shipped this quarter below the pace of the prior two, quotas went to the background. As of Dec 12, Canadian exports were running at 67.3 pct of Oct-Dec quota and 76.1 pct of annual April/March quota.

While the improved action firmed quotes on many items, it still left mills with year-end cleanups on which they were willing to wheel and deal. Boards traded mostly unchanged to higher. Prices flattened on Ponderosa industrials and trading slowed in Western Red Cedar due to the weather and holidays.
